turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: What brings you in today? Patient: I’ve had intermittent flank pain for about five months, and I’ve had several urinary tract infections over the past couple of years. I haven’t had any fever or weight loss, and I haven’t noticed major changes in my urinary or bowel habits.
Can you describe the flank pain in more detail? For example, is it sharp, dull, or crampy, and does it radiate anywhere like to your groin?
“Doctor, the pain feels more like a dull ache than sharp, and it comes and goes rather than being constant. It doesn’t really cramp, and I don’t notice it radiating to my groin.”
Have you noticed any blood in your urine
“Doctor, I haven’t noticed any blood in my urine. I’ve mostly just had that intermittent dull flank ache without any obvious urinary changes.”
How old are you, and do you have any other medical conditions or a family history of kidney problems?
“Doctor, I’m 31 years old, and I don’t have any significant medical conditions besides the recurrent urinary tract infections. I don’t know of any family history of kidney problems.”
Have you ever had any imaging tests of your kidneys, like an ultrasound or a CT scan, during your previous urinary tract infections?
“Doctor, I’ve never had any imaging of my kidneys like an ultrasound or CT scan during my UTIs. It’s mostly been treated with antibiotics when symptoms come up.”
Does the flank pain ever get worse after drinking a large amount of fluids or alcohol?
“Doctor, I haven’t really noticed a clear pattern where the flank pain gets worse after drinking a lot of fluids or alcohol—it seems to come and go without a specific trigger.”
Are you currently experiencing any symptoms of a

“Doctor, right now I’m not having any other symptoms—just the intermittent dull flank ache that comes and goes. I haven’t had fever, chills, or nausea, and I’m not noticing any burning or urgency with urination when the pain happens.”
Have you ever been told you have high blood pressure, or

“Doctor, I’ve never been told I have high blood pressure, and I don’t take any regular medications. I can also say I haven’t noticed any swelling in my legs or face, and I’ve felt generally well aside from the intermittent dull flank ache.”
Have you ever been told what kind of bacteria caused your urinary
“Doctor, I’m not sure what specific bacteria caused my urinary tract infections; I was usually told it was a typical UTI and treated with antibiotics, but I don’t remember the organism name.”
Have you had any recent changes in your vaginal
“Doctor, I haven’t noticed any recent changes in my vagina—no unusual discharge, itching, or bleeding. My main issue has just been the intermittent dull flank ache that comes and goes.”
Have you ever had a kidney stone, or has anyone
“Doctor, I’ve never been told I have a kidney stone, and I don’t think I’ve had one before. No one has mentioned stones on any previous tests either, since I haven’t had kidney imaging.”
Have you noticed any pain or discomfort

“Doctor, during the episodes it’s a dull ache in the flank that’s uncomfortable but not severe, and it comes and goes rather than staying constant. I don’t have burning, urgency, or other urinary discomfort when the pain shows up.”
Have you had any recent trauma or injury to your back
“Doctor, I haven’t had any recent trauma or injury to my back or abdomen. I also haven’t had any other symptoms like fever, rash, joint pain, or shortness of breath.”
Can you tell me if the pain is on the left
“Doctor, the flank pain seems to be on the left side, though it comes and goes so it’s not always in the same exact spot during each episode.”
Does the pain seem to coincide with your menstrual cycle
“Doctor, I haven’t noticed a clear link between the flank pain and my menstrual cycle—it doesn’t seem to reliably start or worsen around my period.”
